chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: Writing a high note for Lamar Wright at Cab Calloway's Cotton Club
summary: Whaley wrote an arrangement for Cab Calloway with a high note that trumpeter Lamar Wright, the iron lip, played.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. Man, he was great, to me. I'd make an arrangement down at the Cotton Club, there, with Cab. And I wrote an arrangement, -- and what was the trumpet player's name? He had a son.

Lamar Wright. And I had Lamar hitting up there in E flat or F, and you know how Cab used to rehearse. He'd play that all the time. So Lamar Wright didn't play it, didn't go up there. He said, 'hey, what's the matter?' He said, 'man, got that single note up there?' He said, well, I can play it. And I said to Cab, man, you're rehearsing, he'd go up there. So he said, 'you put it on paper, didn't
And Cab would say, play it.
Oh, yeah, he could play it, the iron lip.
That's what they used to call him, the iron lip.
